title: DNA scaling results may be suboptimal
description: The learning rate sweep for DNA scaling experiments was on the upper range, and the authors acknowledge it is possible their results are still suboptimal for Mamba.
canonical_description: model performance potentially suboptimal due to incomplete hyperparameter search

evidence.anchor: it is possible that our results are still suboptimal
evidence.quote: (Furthermore, as this LR is on the upper range of the sweep, it is possible that our results are still suboptimal.)

verdict.reasoning: No candidate papers were deep-read, so there is no evidence the gap has been addressed.

ranking.feasibility_reasoning: The gap is narrowly scoped (just rerun scaling experiments with better LR sweeps for Mamba), methodology is standard hyperparameter tuning, and evaluation is clear (perplexity/loss at each scale). Data (e.g., The Pile, C4) is readily available. The main barrier is compute: scaling experiments train models at multiple sizes, and thorough LR sweeps multiply that cost — requiring dozens of training runs, each potentially needing multiple GPUs for days. This is feasible for a well-resourced academic lab or small team with dedicated GPU access, but non-trivial. No fundamental breakthrough needed, but the resource requirements keep it from being highly tractable.
